title: Mitigating Cultural Bias in LLMs via Multi-Agent Cultural Debate
reasoning: The paper focuses on cultural bias in LLMs and proposes a framework to mitigate it through multi-agent debate and a new benchmark (CEBiasBench) across five everyday cultural domains. While cultural personas include values that can touch on moral or religious aspects (e.g., 'religious duty', 'dharma', 'moral duty'), the primary objective and evaluation methods are centered on cultural preferences and representation, not on benchmarking or evaluating specific religious doctrines, moral reasoning frameworks, or ethics systems as a core component. The 'Ethics Statement' section discusses general LLM fairness and stereotyping risks rather than a dedicated evaluation of faith or ethics.
